## Fury Intercepts 9.81 g/t Gold over 2.99 m within Seven Mineralized Zones at Eau Claire, Advancing Resource Conversion


November 24, 2026


[View PDF Version](https://wp-furygoldmines-2024.s3.ca-central-1.amazonaws.com/media/2026/11/23164421/2026-11-24-FURY-News-Release-Revised.pdf)


**TORONTO, Canada – November 24, 2026 – Fury Gold Mines Limited (TSX and NYSE American: FURY) (“Fury” or the “Company”)** is pleased to announce results from five additional drill holes completed as part of the ongoing Phase 2 resource conversion drilling program at the Eau Claire deposit, located in the Eeyou Istchee Territory in the James Bay region of Quebec.


The Phase 2 drilling program is focused on increasing drill density within selected portions of the deposit to support the ongoing Mineral Resource Estimate (“MRE”) update. The objective of the program is to increase geological confidence in areas currently classified as Inferred Mineral Resources and provide information that may contribute to future resource classification upgrades.


**Significant drill highlights, shown in true widths, include:**


- Hole 26EC-134 returned seven mineralized intervals over 103 metres (m) of core, including 9.81 grams per tonne (“g/t”) gold (“Au”) over 2.99 m, 8.55 g/t Au over 1.50 m, and 8.16 g/t Au over 1.00 m
- Hole 26EC-139, drilled approximately 30 m from hole 26EC-134 on the same section, returned 8.33 g/t Au over 2.99 m and 7.30 g/t Au over 1.00 m, supporting the interpretation of geological and grade continuity
- At the eastern extent of the resource, holes 26EC-135 and 26EC-138 intersected 5.69 g/t Au over 1.29 m and 6.33 g/t Au over 2.46 m, respectively, supporting the continuity of high-grade mineralization in an area previously characterized by wider drill spacing


**“Holes 26EC-134 and 26EC-139 were drilled 30 metres apart on the same section, and both returned high-grade intercepts of more than 8 g/t gold over nearly three metres,”** commented Tim Clark, CEO of Fury. **“This kind of consistency is what builds confidence in a resource model. At the same time, holes 26EC-135 and 26EC-138 are tightening up the eastern edge of the deposit, where drilling was previously more widely spaced. With assays pending for another 23 holes, we expect a materially denser dataset to feed the updated Mineral Resource Estimate and, ultimately, the pre-feasibility study.”**


**Implications for Mineral Resource Upgrade**


The drill holes reported in this release were designed to test portions of the current Inferred Mineral Resource where geological continuity has already been demonstrated. Results from holes 26EC-134, and 26EC-139 confirm the continuity of multiple mineralized horizons in the core of the deposit (Figure 2). Holes 26EC-135 and 26EC-138 extend that confidence to the eastern edge of the resource, where drill spacing was previously wider (Figure 3). These results will be incorporated into the updated geological model and the MRE update, which is expected in the coming months. The updated MRE will be an integral part of the ongoing pre-feasibility study (“PFS”) at Eau Claire.


To date, the Phase 2 program has completed 59 holes totalling 28,075 m, of which five holes were abandoned, and two holes are in progress. Assay results are currently pending for 23 holes.

**Sampling and Assaying Disclosure**


Analytical samples for the Drill Program were taken by sawing HQ diameter core into equal halves on site, with one half sent to ALS Chemex in Val D’or, Quebec, Canada for preparation and analysis. All samples were assayed using a 50 g nominal weight fire with assay atomic absorption finish (Au-AA24) and multi-element four acid digest ICP-AES/ICP-MS method (ME-MS61). Where Au-AA24 results were greater than 10 ppm by Au-AA24 were re-assayed with 50 g nominal weight fire assay with gravimetric finish (Au-GRA22). QA/QC programs using internal standard samples and blanks, field and lab duplicates, and lab standards and blanks indicate good overall accuracy and precision.
